claims: Cross-protocol release budgets subtract external recapture before permitting positive internal release.
If external recapture exhausts the shared verified budget, release is blocked.
Any cross-protocol release still inherits the live-execution capability requirement from the role-collapse release gate.
In a two-venue composition, venue B's realized take acts as venue A's external recapture term, so admissibility requires B's take to be below A's shared budget.
Governance-side extraction composes with the other venue's take as an additional recapture term, and can block otherwise admissible paired releases.
Concrete witnesses cover admissible and blocked cross-protocol, two-venue, and governance-timed scenarios.
proof_method: two-venue substitution of realized venue take into external recapture

boundaries: These are local accounting gates, not a complete cross-protocol equilibrium theorem.
Concrete deployments still need to instantiate shared verified budget, venue take, external recapture, and governance extraction from runtime evidence.
The proofs do not select a tokenomics policy; they only constrain when a positive release can be admitted.
The model is not legal, tax, broker-dealer, or securities-law analysis.
